dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: For all natural numbers m and n.
For every real m-by-n matrix A, equivalently A : Fin m -> Fin n -> Real.
For all real parameters fmax and Fmax.
Row indices i range over Fin m and column indices j range over Fin n.
The power-of-two witnesses and selected dyadic exponents range over the integers.
hypotheses: For every row i, r_i = max_{j in Fin n} |A_ij| is strictly positive.
conclusions: For every row i, its computed scale lambda_i is an integer power of two, is strictly positive, and satisfies theta/(2r_i) < lambda_i <= theta/r_i.
For every row i and column j, |lambda_i A_ij| <= theta.
For every row i, there exists a column j, depending on i, such that |lambda_i A_ij| > theta/2.
mathematical_definitions: r_i = LocalDef001(A_i) = max_{j in Fin n} |A_ij|; the equality with a maximum uses n>0.
theta = min(fmax, sqrt(Fmax/n)), where n is cast to a real number.
Because theta/r_i>0, choose an integer e_i satisfying 2^e_i <= theta/r_i < 2^(e_i+1).
D = diag(lambda_i) is the m-by-m diagonal scale matrix.
B = DA = LocalDef003(theta,A), so B_ij = lambda_i A_ij.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Given positive dimensions m and n, an m-by-n real matrix with no zero row in the maximum-absolute-entry sense, and positive real parameters fmax and Fmax, set theta exactly equal to min(fmax, sqrt(Fmax/n)). For each row, choose the dyadic scale lambda_i = 2^e_i corresponding to the half-open dyadic interval containing theta divided by that row's maximum absolute entry. Then every lambda_i is positive and lies strictly above theta/(2r_i) and at or below theta/r_i. Consequently, every entry of the exactly row-scaled matrix diag(lambda_i)A has absolute value at most theta, while each scaled row has at least one entry whose absolute value is strictly greater than theta/2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is an implication chain. If any stated positivity hypothesis fails, the proposition holds vacuously and asserts no scaling properties for that input.
The assumptions m>0 and n>0 prevent empty row and column index types; in particular, the per-row existential column conclusion is not vacuous.
The positive-row hypothesis excludes every all-zero row and makes every denominator r_i nonzero.
Since n, fmax, and Fmax are positive, Fmax/n, its square root, and theta are positive, so the positive branch of LocalDef007 is always used.
The exponent is selected noncomputably by Classical.choose. The declaration specifies its interval property but not an executable selection procedure.
All quantities and operations are exact real-number operations. No floating-point format, rounding operation, overflow, underflow, representability constraint, or computed approximation is encoded.
The parameters fmax and Fmax are only assumed to be positive reals; no additional relationship or machine-level interpretation is imposed.
No bound is imposed directly on the original entries beyond requiring every row to contain a nonzero entry.
The strict lower conclusion is existential per row: the witnessing column may differ from one row to another.
ambiguities: The proof term passed to Classical.choose is elided in the displayed body of LocalDef007, but D009 specifies the witness property. The selected integer is therefore abstract rather than computationally identified.
